Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you in any way. We’ll use a quick screening tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s 10 gentle questions about the past seven days; it helps us spot moms who might need a little extra support with mood or anxiety, and it includes a question about self-harm so we can keep you safe. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone’s in danger. We’ll go at your pace, and you can pause any time. Ready for the first question?  

Over the past week, have you still been able to look forward to things you used to enjoy, or has that sense of enjoyment slipped away?

I still get excited about a few things—like when my sister drops off coffee or when the baby gives me one of those big gummy smiles—but mostly the “spark” feels lower. It’s like I can enjoy stuff for a minute, then it fades faster than it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Most of the time I can still laugh—like yesterday my husband made a silly joke and I caught myself giggling—but it feels a little forced, like the laugh doesn’t come as easily or last as long as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to a couple of things—like tomorrow I’m planning to push the stroller to the park—but it’s more “that’ll be nice” than the excited buzz I used to feel. The enjoyment is there, just dimmer.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

I catch myself doing that, yeah. Like if the baby won’t settle, part of me wonders if I’m missing some technique or if my milk’s not good enough. I usually shake it off pretty fast, but it still pops up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll just feel this little knot in my stomach, even when everything’s calm—like I’ll suddenly worry the baby’s breathing sounds different or that I forgot to lock the door. It passes pretty quickly, but it shows up out of nowhere a couple of times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not full-on panicky, but once or twice this week I felt my heart race and had this sudden “something’s not right” feeling—like a little wave of dread. It lasted maybe a minute or two, then faded.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. Like yesterday, the baby wouldn’t nap and the laundry pile looked huge, and for a minute I felt like I was drowning. I still get everything done, but it feels heavier—like I’m juggling with one more ball than I have hands for.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
Not really. I’m mostly tired enough to fall asleep once my head hits the pillow. Once in a while I’ll lie there thinking about the next day, but I still drift off within maybe 20 minutes.
I have felt sad or miserable
Yeah, I’d say I feel sad a few days a week—kind of like a gray cloud hanging around even when nothing’s really wrong. It’s not all day, but it comes and goes.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried twice this week—once when the baby wouldn’t latch and once when I dropped a plate and it shattered. The tears came fast, then stopped, but yeah, I’ve had those “I just need to cry” moments.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, that hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Symptoms endorsed  
- Dys­phoria: intermittent “gray-cloud” sadness several days/week; two crying spells  
- Anhedonia: enjoyment markedly reduced (“dimmer”) but present  
- Subjective guilt: transient self-blame when baby fusses  
- Anxious arousal: daily unprovoked worry, brief heart-racing/dread episodes (1–2×/wk)  
- Feeling overwhelmed: tasks “feel heavier,” occasional “drowning” sensation  
- Sleep: no significant insomnia (falls asleep ≤20 min)  

Pattern  
Mild-to-moderate mood distress with prominent anxiety; functioning maintained but effortful. No anhedonic total loss, no self-harm ideation.

Screening significance  
Meets partial criteria for minor postpartum depression ± comorbid anxiety; score suggests subsyndromal distress requiring close follow-up. No safety red flags at present.

Plan  
Provide scoring, psycho-education, offer follow-up screening in 2 weeks; if symptoms worsen, formal evaluation for PPD/PPA.
